prediction.evidence: Data: arithmetic, colour, continent and yes/no-type questions with a user guess, same answer format in both models. Main evidence: the final-layer heads of A copy in-context answer tokens more than matched controls (all four L17 heads; L17H0 also attends more to them; L17H2 suppresses less), and this is specific to the actual English answer words (L17 mean colours +1.80, numbers +0.37) rather than their foreign translations (+0.37, -0.94), as repeating the user's guess with tied embeddings would require. Secondary: A's associations weakened mainly in the answer domains (numbers, colours) versus unrelated relations, consistent with outputs pushed toward wrong guesses, though controls show this is domain-wide. Cue-context attention, cue marking and some L15/L16 number copying lean the other way, and effects are small, so the probability is about 0.6.
